subject: Streaming pauses + connection throttle causing partial chunks and 504 spikes
messages:
From: Tim Keller <tim.keller@clearviewanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearView DevOps <devops@clearviewanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:18:00 -0400
Subject: Streaming stalls + 504 spike during peak - urgent

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing repeated streaming stalls across our live transcript clients this morning (around 15:10 EDT). The behavior: the WebSocket stream sends the first few chunks, then the connection goes silent for 6-12s, followed by a 504 from the edge/load balancer. Some clients receive partial final chunks (truncated JSON) which breaks our consumer logic. Error rate for streaming endpoints spiked from ~0.5% to ~18% during the first hour of the incident.

Impact: live captions dropped for ~20% of sessions; our customer success teams are getting alerts and customers are complaining. We also noticed a correlated CPU spike on our side and a sudden number of TCP RSTs from the client NAT IP pool.

Attached a small logs-snippet.txt with request ids and timestamps (request ids prefixed CV-). Happy to jump on a bridge — we have an on-call starting in 10 minutes.

Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood-side or an intermediate proxy issue? We use the hosted Redwood API for this workload (no Dedicated).

Thanks,
Tim
Director, Platform Engineering
ClearView Analytics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tim Keller <tim.keller@clearviewanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:25:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Streaming stalls + 504 spike during peak - urgent

Tim — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m escalating this to our SE and AE right away and we’ll open an incident.

Immediate asks so we can triage faster:
- Can you paste one full request id (e.g. CV-XXXXX) from the logs you attached?
- Were the affected sessions using streaming via WebSocket or chunked HTTP transfer (we need the client header: Upgrade: websocket or Transfer-Encoding: chunked)?
- Any recent infra or proxy changes on your side?

Short-term mitigations we can try while investigating:
- Route affected clients to our fallback endpoint (non-streaming / polling) — we can flip this for a subset to reduce errors.
- If you control an edge proxy (nginx/ALB), try disabling proxy buffering and increasing keepalive/accept backlog temporarily.

I’ve scheduled a short bridge at this Zoom link: https://zoom.us/j/999888777 — Jordan, will you join? Rishi, I’m looping you for account context and credits if this is service-impacting.

— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Tim Keller <tim.keller@clearviewanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 17:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Streaming stalls + 504 spike during peak - urgent

Tim / Soojin — I pulled the request IDs you sent and matched them to our ingress logs. Quick findings:

- Ingress behavior: connections from CV IP range show rapid accept -> partial writes -> prolonged socket-level write stalls (~6–12s) before connection reset. Our edge returns 504 when upstream does not flush within our request timeout window.
- Load balancer health checks did not indicate node death; however, the worker process that handles streaming (continuous batching path) shows a backlog growth pattern: KV cache flushes + large prefix outputs led to sustained syscall write() waits.
- We also see an anomalous number of FIN/RST from the client NATs during the stalls.

Hypothesis: intermediate proxy (client or CV edge) plus our recent connection backpressure change combined to create a tight socket write backlog. Nginx (if present) may be buffering chunked responses or enforcing proxy_timeouts causing writeback pressure.

Quick mitigations I recommend (order matters):
1) Ask ClearView to set proxy_buffering off for the streaming endpoint and increase proxy_read_timeout to 90s. (If they can’t, we can route them to a different hostname that avoids their proxy.)
2) On our side: temporarily increase write timeout and accept backlog on the streaming pool and disable the aggressive per-connection rate limiter that recently landed in prod (roll back INF-4807).
3) If immediate fix is needed, route affected traffic to a non-streaming fallback (short-term) for 10% of sessions to reduce blast radius.

Attached: nginx-config-diff.txt (example diff), runtime-metrics.png (backlog timeline). I’ll start a hotfix branch for the rate-limiter rollback now.

— Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tim Keller <tim.keller@clearviewanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 02:14:00 -04:00
Subject: Executive escalation: ClearView streaming outage impact and recommended remediation

Marissa / Rishi — escalating for exec attention and prioritization. Summary:
- Customer: ClearView Analytics (large platform customer; active trial -> enterprise expansion).
- Incident: streaming sessions intermittently stall leading to increased 504s and truncated chunk payloads. Significant customer impact to live-UX during their peak window.
- Root cause (current hypothesis): interaction between our recent connection backpressure change (INF-4807) and ClearView’s edge proxy buffering which created socket-level backpressure and led to blocked writes on our streaming workers.

Business asks:
1) Prioritize the rollback hotfix (Jordan has branch). Need approval for a T+1 deploy to staging and immediate rollback to prod if tests pass.
2) Approve a temporary SLA credit (recommended 10% of September bill) if the postmortem confirms service degradation attributable to our runtime change.
3) Communicate to ClearView a timeline and the mitigation actions we’ve taken.

I’ve included the incident Jira: INF-4821 and PagerDuty: PD-83472. Jordan will provide technical notes; I can own customer comms.

— Soojin

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tim Keller <tim.keller@clearviewanalytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Streaming stalls + 504 spike during peak - urgent

Tim — quick update and next steps (we appreciate your patience):

What we did:
- Applied temporary routing to a fallback streaming pool for 30% of traffic initiating after 09:00 UTC to reduce write pressure.
- Jordan rolled a short-term rollback of INF-4807 to remove the aggressive per-connection rate cap; results: error rate on the affected sessions dropped from ~18% -> ~1.8% within 30m.
- Recommended configuration change for your edge: set proxy_buffering off and increase proxy_read_timeout to 90s (see nginx-config-diff.txt we attached). If you want, we can provide the exact snippet to your ops team.

Next steps:
- We will run a controlled deploy of the staged hotfix to prod in the next 2 hours and monitor for regressions.
- Postmortem draft (postmortem-draft.md) will be shared by EOD tomorrow; it will include root cause, timeline, mitigations, and our credit proposal.

Credit/compensation: Rishi and Marissa are evaluating an appropriate account credit. Initial recommendation: 10% credit for September pro-rated to impacted usage.

Can you confirm whether you’re able to apply the proxy change on your side? If not, we’ll keep the fallback routing until the hotfix is fully validated.

Thanks again for flagging this quickly — Jordan and I will stay on the bridge until you confirm traffic looks normal.

— Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
